sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Pramara is a promotional-product and toy/OEM supplier with design, sourcing, manufacturing and fulfilment capabilities. Its strongest positive is growing operating sales and EBIT alongside established corporate relationships. The decisive negative is capital tied up in receivables, supplier advances and other-party loans despite repeated equity funding. At ₹87, a modest reported P/E does not automatically compensate for cash and asset-verification uncertainty. This is a financing-dependent growth/special-situation watchlist, not an established compounder. Research Hold: obtain independent asset confirmations, reconciled cash and related-party bridges and a credible funded expansion plan before ordinary valuation or ranking. A price decline alone does not clear these gates.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Pramara Promotions Limited; NSE PRAMARA; ISIN INE0O7A01017; SME at the 20 October 2026 cutoff. Quote ₹87 at the 19 October close; issued shares 13,944,168; market capitalization ₹121.31cr. Group financials through 31 March 2026 follow Accounting Standards (AS) under the Companies Accounting Standards Rules, not Ind AS. The valuation begins on 20 October 2026 using the preceding authenticated close and ends on 20 October 2031, with exact days divided by 365.2425 and a 15% nominal pre-personal-tax INR equity hurdle. The ₹5lakh reference position is a liquidity convention, not personalized sizing. Gates: G1 Conditional, G2 material Hold, G3 Conditional, G4 Conditional. Confidence is high in exchange identity/count/lot, medium in reported income, medium-low in pledge disclosure, and low in collectible assets and isolated incremental organic returns. Restored rating cooperation supports funding access but does not independently confirm the asset balances.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 factor scores are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 1, BAL 4, EXEC 4, EARN 4, R NS, D 3, P NS and L 5. BQS has known contribution 3.88, 88% coverage and diagnostic bounds 4.00–5.08. GQS has known contribution 4.50, 85% coverage and raw diagnostic bounds 4.65–6.00, reduced to 4.65–5.00 by the persistent CASH≤3 cap. Both points remain NS. IAS has known contribution 1.10 and 30% coverage, with no valid point. Missing weights are never renormalized or given midpoint scores. All ranking flags are false because G2 is a material Hold. Exact Decimal contributions and evidence-linked anchors follow. A complete two-factor ±1 GOV/DUR grid shows uncertainty without imputing missing CAP or creating a new score; no cell clears the evidence gate.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Corporate clients buy campaign-specific premiums, toys, gifts and branded merchandise. Pramara combines concept/design, licensing assistance, tooling, sourcing, moulding/assembly, testing, packaging and distribution. Economics depend on repeat projects, mix, procurement and delivery accuracy rather than consumer subscriptions. FY26 group sales of ₹112.46cr comprise ₹103.42cr local sales, ₹7.38cr exports and ₹1.66cr services. The separate FOB forex note is not the same geography definition. Receivables and advance-funded sourcing mean recognized sales can precede cash by months. HK and US subsidiaries and a 40% associate do not establish global pricing power. The 70%-owned toy JV receives no speculative modeled earnings. Factory-in-factory equipment access is not ownership of every machine. No audited SKU margin, order-level collection or product-unit series was found, so no fabricated unit economics or utilization is used.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is qualification by large consumer brands, design-to-delivery coordination, mould/process experience and repeat execution. These capabilities can reduce client coordination costs but do not prove exclusivity or pricing power. The top ten customers were 73.30% of FY23 sales and the top ten suppliers 72.16%; no current quantitative concentration bridge was found despite a rating description of diversified clients. Campaign spending is discretionary, while major clients own the consumer brands and can renegotiate or dual-source. Resin prices and freight can move ahead of pass-through. OK Play is a relevant listed operating comparison in toys and contract plastics but also has institutional and automotive exposure. Funskool is a branded/licensing/distribution comparator without a clean listed toy multiple. Archies is an adjacent retail/corporate-gift competitor with different brand and cash-cycle economics. No indiscriminate peer-P/E average is used.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The preselected five-year FY21–FY26 window has five intervals: revenue rose from ₹40.7831cr to ₹112.4565cr, a 22.49% CAGR. The three-year FY23–FY26 comparison is ₹50.0628cr to ₹112.4565cr, a 30.97% CAGR. Absolute annual additions are retained below. FY21 was 36.31% below the FY20 contextual revenue of ₹64.0339cr; the six-year contextual CAGR is 9.84%. This supports the single base-distortion adjustment from the numerical REV anchor of 8 to 7, with no second small-base penalty. Retrieved reports show no material acquired-business sales explaining the expansion, but physical volume versus price/mix is not disclosed: nominal underlying operating sales are not audited volume growth. H1FY26 revenue grew approximately 72.88%; derived H2FY26 grew only 6.50%. The H1 statement includes no current tax provision, making half-year PAT extrapolation misleading. No sustained-acceleration bonus is awarded. Client wins, licensing and domestic sourcing provide a plausible path, not guaranteed order conversion.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Bottom-up expansion requires retained corporate programs, additional qualified designs/campaigns, reliable tooling and factory access, supplier finance and collections. It cannot be inferred from a national toy-market forecast. The ₹50cr June 2026 order book cited by CRISIL is an order stock, not collected revenue or a five-year annuity. FY26 supplier advances increased by ₹20.44cr, other-party loans by ₹18.51cr, and ₹9.40cr was deployed to land. These uses compete with funding for the toy operation. The FY23–FY26 financing-side incremental normalized NOPAT/invested-capital proxy is approximately 6.86%. Removing separately identified other-party loan growth raises the diagnostic toward 8.7%, still not a demonstrated high-return organic cohort. The equity hurdle is not mechanically the same as an operating cost of capital; the comparison identifies weak economics, not a precise spread. Asset confirmation, investment timing and subsidiary scope prevent a clean project return, so CAP remains NS. GQS remains NS with a diagnostic ceiling of 5 because cash conversion is persistently weak. Model growth of 0/10/18% is linked to working capital, capex and interest; all three unrescued paths breach the cash reserve rather than receiving free funding.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Capital raised is not itself business value created. Shares increased from 6.611m before the IPO, adjusted for the earlier bonus, to 9.035m, 10.971m and 13.944m across FY24–26. March promoter holding is 32.1954%, but its filing contradicts itself: the quantitative table reports 1.667m pledged shares, 37.1247% of promoter holding, while the declaration says No. The ₹177.39cr May proposal was withdrawn on May 29 and contributes no financing. The earlier 295,000 warrants at ₹169 are out of the money against ₹87 and are not assumed to exercise. June 2024 guidance for FY25 sales growth of 60–70% and EBITDA margin improvement of 200bp delivered 36.13% growth and a 131bp margin decline. Related-party purchases/reimbursements of ₹19.16cr and disclosed creditor balances of ₹6.84cr require reconciliation against group total creditors of ₹4.42cr. FY25 CARO said loan repayment and interest schedules were not stipulated; FY26 CARO says schedules are stipulated, nothing overdue and no loans lacking specified terms. This is an improvement in documented terms, not proof that all outstanding loans are collectible. Favorable IFC and secretarial conclusions and no reported lender default or fraud are counterevidence. No allegation of diversion or fraud is made.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The complete six-year group table, interim rows and formulas are embedded below. FY26 operating EBIT excluding other income and associate profit is ₹15.6403cr. Subtract recurring CSR of ₹0.0925cr, finance cost of ₹7.2991cr and normalize tax at 25% to obtain PAT of approximately ₹6.1865cr, versus reported ₹10.0355cr. Other income of ₹3.8425cr includes ₹2.4369cr interest and a ₹1.3214cr creditor writeback. Three-year reported CFO/PAT is −3.43 and five-year is −2.34; disclosed debt and other-loan reclassifications still leave poor recent conversion. The later annual cash flow mechanically fixes an earlier omitted ₹15.4893cr subtotal and relocates ₹3.3688cr short-debt movement. The earlier mismatch is therefore not a current missing-cash claim. The remaining ₹1.8871cr increase in other current assets appears as a cash inflow, a ₹3.7742cr sign sensitivity requiring a reconciled bridge. Land use is traced; separate other-party loans remain collection-risk assets. Recourse factoring is grossed up on both sides. Total cash of ₹6.09cr is not fully available: the unrestricted proxy is ₹2.99cr, then the land earmark leaves ₹2.39cr. Cash and current accounts alone are ₹0.8942cr. AS operating rent remains in EBIT and is not capitalized into invented Ind AS lease debt. RPT classification and independent confirmations remain material evidence gaps. A visually checked standalone loan-note amount of ₹24.7983cr agrees with CARO; an OCR column omission was not treated as a company discrepancy.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹87, market capitalization is ₹121.31cr, reported P/E 12.09× and normalized P/E approximately 19.61×. The published March balance-sheet bridge produces grossed-up EV of ₹169.53cr before speculative loan recoveries, about 10.09× normalized EBITDA. These are explicitly mixed-date book-snapshot multiples, not a claim that March cash equals October cash. Separate October entry cash, debt, shares and signed cash-surplus bridges are retained for each scenario. Other loans are valued through dated collections only, never deducted at par from EV and counted again in cash. The terminal multiple applies to earned trailing-12-month EBITDA ending 20 October 2031, not the endpoint annualized revenue run-rate or future cash. The operating model uses terminal EBITDA multiples of 7/10/13×, revenue growth of 0/10/18%, EBIT margins of 9/13.5/15%, and operating working capital of 1.25/1.07/0.85 times sales. These are analyst scenarios, not authenticated peer fair-value multiples. All unrescued cases fail a conservative pre-receipt funding trough, and G2 independently suppresses ordinary returns and actionable targets. Rescue cases issue whole shares at 80% of the trial entry price with 2% fees at the start of each interval. They prefund capital expenditure, working-capital investment, interest, principal, cash tax and legacy obligations before receipts. Conditional rescue IRRs and 12/15/18% hurdle-entry solvers remain separate from IAS. Linked reverse-working-capital solvers identify the collection/asset-turn improvement needed for the 15% hurdle, and linked reverse-growth solvers rerun funding, dilution, working capital and capex for the hurdle and 5×/10× wealth targets. Two-way growth/working-capital, margin/multiple, recovery/reserve, credit/interest and capex/working-capital grids are embedded, alongside cash-accessibility, RPT-claim and principal-payment tests.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest positive counterargument is that domestic manufacturing expansion, repeat blue-chip clients and eventual inventory/advance conversion will turn the enlarged asset base into cash. CRISIL restored cooperation and assesses near-term liquidity as adequate. That may prove right, but receipts must be demonstrated rather than assumed. The linked bear case assumes no sales growth, a 9% EBIT margin, working capital of 1.25 times sales, only 25% recovery of other loans in 2028, full settlement of ₹3.3457cr contingencies and scheduled debt amortization. Positive operating income can still coexist with financing needs, dilution and permanent per-share loss. A customer or other-loan writeoff reduces recoverable equity; an unfulfilled supplier advance delays both production and collections. RPT-claim tests do not automatically add balances already included in creditors. A modeled pre-entry cash-floor breach is not asserted as an observed default: it exposes a missing funded bridge between the March accounts and the quote date. The decisive variable is independently verified conversion of ₹25.22cr other loans and ₹81.81cr net receivables plus supplier advances, not headline PAT growth.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5× wealth requires about 38% annual per-share compounding and 10× requires about 58.5%. That is harder than growing revenue when working capital starts near annual sales and financing dilutes ownership. Static undiluted market capitalizations of ₹606.57cr for 5× or ₹1,213.14cr for 10× are not forecasts and omit new shares. The linked reverse engine instead targets ₹435/₹870 terminal value per share after scenario rescue and fees. It varies EBIT margins across 10/13.5/16% and searches 0–100% annual revenue growth for a finite supported crossing. Any supported result retains required revenue, terminal shares, financing and residual; absent crossings stay unavailable rather than extrapolated. This business has not demonstrated asset turns, incremental returns or retained cash sufficient for a 5×/10× compounder designation without optimistic recoveries and refinancing.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Obtain counterparty confirmations and repayment dates for ₹25.2169cr other loans. Collection of 60% by March 2027 is a base-case assumption, not guidance. 2. Reconcile ₹57.9832cr net receivables, ₹9.91cr factoring and ₹23.8306cr supplier advances; approximately ₹9.02cr receivables are older than six months. 3. Explain RPT creditors of ₹6.8406cr versus total creditors of ₹4.4155cr and the other-current-asset cash-flow sign. 4. Monitor free cash after restrictions and earmarks against a ₹1cr operating reserve and ₹4–5.5cr annual repayments; authenticate renewals and undrawn facilities. 5. Require positive post-interest cash realization, not merely additional equity; three-year reported CFO is negative ₹68.30cr. 6. Compare the next like-for-like half-year with H2FY26 growth of 6.50%, normalized margins and taxes. 7. Verify land ownership, advance completion and the remaining ₹0.60cr allocation; no speculative retail/US/JV contribution before operating evidence. 8. Verify current pledges, promoter ownership and any exercise of the 295,000 warrants. 9. Treat migration as effective only after exchange approval and effective trading notice. 10. Recheck live depth, surveillance and whole-lot exit capacity before implementation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Research Hold: financing-dependent growth and governance-evidence watchlist. This is not a verified compounder or an ordinary value purchase merely because reported P/E is 12×. Missing CAP leaves BQS and GQS unavailable, and material G2 Hold independently excludes all numerical rankings. Missing R, P and derived Q leave IAS unavailable. G3 Conditional recognizes a public rating assessment of adequate liquidity rather than alleging an actual default. G4 Conditional recognizes authenticated daily trading and a 500-share lot rather than assuming that every SME is untradeable. First reconcile assets, RPTs and cash; then rerun a credible funded base case and stress; only then apply price and return hurdles. A lower price reduces an incoming investor's cost but can increase recapitalization dilution. It cannot make unconfirmed assets collectible. No personalized position size or execution recommendation is implied.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source and claim registers map the analysis to exact-issuer originals and page locators. Full annual audit reports, CARO, IFC, audit-trail statements, group other matters and financial notes were reviewed, not only headline results. The website's FY20-labelled file actually contains FY21 accounts; its FY20 comparative is used only as context. Rupee amounts are divided by 10,000,000 and lakh amounts by 100 to obtain INR crore. CFO/PAT uses aggregate flows, not an average of annual ratios. Operating EBIT excludes other income and associate profit. The funding-side invested-capital proxy is equity including warrant money plus book debt less reported cash and investments; it is not isolated organic project capital. Forward cash gross-ups recourse factoring consistently, excludes restricted cash and the land earmark, pays old tax/statutory/gratuity and contingencies once, and counts retained cash once in terminal equity. Monthly pre-receipt trough tests are conservative scenario diagnostics, not authenticated daily cash records. Material open questions are asset confirmations, loan terms and collection, related-party netting, pledge contradictions, land completion, product-level returns, current customer concentration and complete cutoff surveillance. The retained extracts preserve facts and provenance without redistributing whole reports or individual personal identifiers.

conventions: Gross up both receivables and debt for factored bills; do not add factoring again as a separate claim.
Cash excludes pledged and government deposits and 0.60 land earmark. That earmark alone funds remaining land cost; 9.40 already paid is never paid twice.
Opening other-party loans are nonoperating recoverable assets, not operating revenue. Recoveries are separately dated and no uncollected interest is compounded.
AS rent remains in EBIT; future rent and principal are not both deducted. Terminal operational land/property receives no separate value.
Restricted deposits retained until terminal and recovered only at scenario recovery rate after factoring debt remains in terminal claims.
Old tax/statutory, gratuity and contingent cash settlements are separate from forward tax. Tax asset refunds are limited, uncertain and explicitly timed.
No withdrawn May 2026 raise proceeds. Outstanding 2025 warrants are excluded from ordinary financeability; separate conversion test only.
No acquisition or NCI claim assumed silently: published 70% subsidiary is pre-operating; scenarios model legacy group, with no toy-JV earnings uplift or unpriced minority profits.
No dividends. All retained generated cash remains once in terminal equity.

summary: Pramara is a promotional-product and toy/OEM supplier with design, sourcing, manufacturing and fulfilment capabilities. Its strongest positive is growing operating sales and EBIT alongside established corporate relationships. The decisive negative is capital tied up in receivables, supplier advances and other-party loans despite repeated equity funding.
